description:
**Three targets, three toolchains, and nothing gating any of them.** There is no `verify.sh` content, no CI, and no test anywhere in the repository.

This is `unblock` in the strict sense: it ships no capability. Its value is that every later tasklist can fail loudly, and that the compile-clean state won `10`–`30` cannot silently rot.

**The honest constraint, stated up front:** the authoring machine has Swift 6.2 but **no JDK, no Gradle, no Android SDK, and no Xcode** (Command Line Tools only). So `verify.sh` must degrade explicitly — running what it can, and **reporting what it skipped and why**, never silently passing a target it could not build. A gate that quietly skips is worse than no gate, because it reads as green.

userStories.title: `.chief/verify.sh` builds and tests every target it can reach
userStories.description: Swift, Gradle and TypeScript, each gated on its toolchain being present.
acceptanceCriteria: `.chief/verify.sh` runs the Swift build and tests, the Gradle build, and the TS typecheck.
A missing toolchain produces an explicit SKIPPED line naming the toolchain and what went unverified — never a silent pass.
It exits non-zero if any reachable target fails to build.
It exits non-zero on a deliberately broken tree — proven, not assumed.

userStories.title: CI builds all three targets on a runner that has the toolchains
userStories.description: What the laptop cannot verify, CI must. This is the only place Android is genuinely checked.
acceptanceCriteria: A CI workflow builds iOS (macOS runner), Android (JDK + SDK) and the RN package.
The Android job is a REQUIRED check — it is the only environment where that target is compiled at all.
CI fails on a warning regression in the Swift target, which is currently at zero.
